description: Add the two server actions that create and decide attendance requests to the hr-requests edge function, following the exact patterns of apply_leave/decide_leave/decide_remote: JWT->employee resolution for the employee action, admin-only gating for the decision, per-type validation via the shared pure rules, overlap/duplicate guards, best-effort notifications on create and on decision, and the per-type on-approval effect on the attendance row. Also add a cancel path for the employee's own pending request. The edge function remains the ONLY writer of attendance_requests and of the attendance-row effects.
steps: Edit supabase/functions/hr-requests/index.ts. Import the new helpers from ../_shared/attendance-rules.ts: validateAttendanceRequest, regularizedAttendance, plus the already-imported istParts/addDays/normalizeSchedules and whatever closeDay/windowMinutes dependencies the helpers need (they are self-contained, so you mainly import the two new functions and type).

Add employee action `apply_attendance_request`: resolve the employee from auth.uid()->employees.profile_id exactly like apply_leave (reuse the same employee lookup block; a single lookup can serve apply_leave/cancel_leave/apply_attendance_request/cancel_attendance_request). Read type/work_date/to_date/reason/requested times from the body. Load hr_settings.day_schedules (normalizeSchedules) for the day's schedule. Call validateAttendanceRequest with today = istParts(new Date()).date and minutes-since-midnight parsed from any requested HH:MM times; on {ok:false} return fail(message). Guard duplicates/overlap: reject if the employee already has a pending or approved attendance_request of the same type covering the same work_date (for WFH, overlapping the from/to range), mirroring the leave overlap check. For absence_clarification / missed_login_regularization, additionally sanity-check against the attendance table: a missed_login_regularization should target a day the employee did NOT already have a completed attendance row for (or had only an action_needed/open row) — document the chosen rule; an absence_clarification should target a day with no present attendance (i.e. an absent day) — if the data clearly contradicts, return a helpful fail message, but keep it lenient rather than blocking edge cases. Insert the row with the service role, select('*'). Then notifyAdmins with a type-specific title/body/details and path '/hrms/approvals', cta 'Review in CRM' (mirror the apply_leave notify block; include Employee, Date/Range, Type label, Reason, and for missed-login the requested login/logout times). Return json({ ok: true, request: created }).

Add employee action `cancel_attendance_request`: update attendance_requests set status='cancelled' where id=body.id AND employee_id=employee.id AND status='pending', select id; return ok on success else fail('Only a pending request of yours can be cancelled.') — identical shape to cancel_leave.

Add admin action `decide_attendance_request`: gate on isAdmin (403 for non-admins, like decide_leave). Load the pending request by id (status='pending') with the employee relation (employees(profile_id, first_name, last_name, employee_code)). If not found, fail('That request is no longer pending.'). Set status approved/rejected + admin_note + decided_by/decided_at. THEN apply the on-approval effect ONLY when approve is true, per type: (a) work_from_home -> ensure the attendance row for that work_date (range: each date) is marked remote-approved. Prefer to REUSE the existing attendance remote columns so the reactive flow and command center stay consistent: upsert/update the attendance row setting work_mode='remote', remote_status='approved', remote_reason (from the request), remote_decided_by/at; if no attendance row exists for a future/absent WFH day, create a minimal remote-approved row (work_date, employee_id, remote_status='approved', work_mode='remote') so the day counts — match the column shape used by attendance-punch. Keep backward-compatible with decide_remote (do not remove or change it). (b) missed_login_regularization -> compute the corrected fields with regularizedAttendance using the day's snapshotted schedule (or today's schedule for that weekday as a fallback, exactly like attendance-punch does) and UPDATE/INSERT the attendance row's first_login_at/last_logout_at/open_since(null)/worked_minutes/window_minutes/status/is_late/late_minutes/overtime_minutes/schedule snapshot. This is the point-in-time effect that MUST go through the shared pure rules. (c) absence_clarification -> record the justification: store nothing on attendance beyond the request itself (the approved request IS the record), i.e. no attendance mutation; the approval simply resolves the clarification. In all three, notifyUser(profileOf(row.employees), ...) with a type-specific decision title/body and path '/attendance', cta 'Open My Attendance' (mirror decide_leave). Return json({ ok: true }).

Keep every reply as 200 {ok:true,...} or 200 {ok:false,message}; non-2xx only for faults/forbidden, exactly as the file already does. Do not alter apply_leave/cancel_leave/decide_leave/decide_remote/email_salary_slip behavior.
Extend src/lib/attendance-client.ts only if needed — hrRequest() is generic and already handles the new actions; no change may be required. If you add typed helper wrappers, keep them additive.

Add a read helper to src/lib/attendance-queries.ts: fetchAttendanceRequests({ employeeId?, status? }) returning AttendanceRequest[] via hrmsDb().from('attendance_requests'), mirroring fetchLeaves (RLS already scopes employees to their own rows). This is consumed by the UI in FEAT-005.

Type-check the edge function with `npx -y deno check supabase/functions/hr-requests/index.ts` (download Deno via npm; delete any deno.lock it leaves behind). Run `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` and `bun run test` to confirm the lib changes compile and the byte-identical rules test still passes.
acceptance_criteria: hr-requests/index.ts handles apply_attendance_request, cancel_attendance_request and decide_attendance_request with the same validation/gating/notification shape as the leave actions, and still handles all pre-existing actions unchanged.

apply_attendance_request validates via the shared validateAttendanceRequest, rejects duplicates/overlaps, inserts the row, and notifies admins; cancel only cancels the caller's own pending row; decide is admin-only.

On approval: WFH marks/creates the attendance row as remote-approved (reusing the existing remote_* columns, leaving decide_remote intact); missed_login_regularization recomputes the attendance row via regularizedAttendance (shared rules); absence_clarification resolves without corrupting attendance. Each decision notifies the employee.
`npx deno check` on the edge function passes (no type errors).
verification: `npx -y deno check supabase/functions/hr-requests/index.ts` reports no errors (deno.lock cleaned up afterward).
`bun run test` passes (byte-identical rules guard still green).

Re-read the decide_attendance_request block and confirm the attendance-row effects use the shared pure helpers and reuse the existing remote_* columns rather than introducing a parallel WFH mechanism.
